action: Port users and shippers should use only channels announced by the Autoridade Portuária de Santos and the Federal Police, and treat unexpected emails or calls about cargo, access or payments with caution.
date_note: Systems went down on 6 November; the ransom demand was reported on 17 November, which is the date used here.
exec: Santos port authority says a group that claimed an attack on its systems tried to negotiate a ransom and got no reply.
impact: Website and administrative systems down since 6 November; port operations continued, per APS. About 70% of affected files recovered from backups; no ransom amount was reported.
plain: Brazil's Port of Santos authority says a group that claimed an attack on its systems tried to negotiate a ransom and got no reply. It says about 70% of affected files were recovered from backups.

key_findings: Baguete (10 Nov): APS confirmed a cyberattack on port systems, down since the morning of 6 Nov; it first cited a power outage hitting its servers and had not determined scale or whether data was accessed.
Cesportos raised the port protection level to II; the Federal Police office in Santos said it had been notified but had received no documents or opened an inquiry.

O POVO (17 Nov): APS confirmed it received a ransom demand from hackers claiming the attack; preliminary investigation points to action from outside Brazil; a report is being prepared for the Federal Police.
APS says data was kept in backups and is being recovered, and believes the virus had been present since at least 6 Nov.

Revista Oeste (12 Nov, relaying APS president Anderson Pomini via Metropoles): a group that claimed the attack tried to negotiate a ransom, got no reply and no terms were set; APS has not confirmed a criminal intrusion; about 70% of affected files recovered from backups; Federal Police opened an inquiry on Tuesday (the article gives no date).

summary: Santos Port Authority (APS) systems have been down since 6 November. Revista Oeste (12 November) quotes APS president Anderson Pomini saying a group claiming the attack tried to negotiate a ransom and got no reply, and that APS has not confirmed a criminal intrusion; Baguete (10 November) says APS confirmed a cyberattack. About 70% of affected files were recovered from backups. Sources differ on a Federal Police inquiry.
title: Santos port authority: group contacted it about a ransom after systems went down on 6 November; APS says the group got no reply

validation.note: Verify desk read all four pages. Conflicts kept in the summary: Federal Police inquiry (Oeste 12 Nov says opened; Baguete 10 Nov says none yet; O POVO 17 Nov says APS is preparing a report for the PF); O POVO says APS confirmed receiving a ransom demand and a foreign origin, while Oeste says APS has not confirmed a criminal intrusion and Pomini points to a power failure. DGABC (12 Nov) supports 70% of backups recovered. Sources truly conflict.

review.note: Compared with O POVO, Baguete, Oeste, DGABC: title said APS 'did not engage' (Oeste: no reply), now 'got no reply'; summary now gives Baguete (APS confirmed a cyberattack) vs Oeste (not confirmed a criminal intrusion); inquiry date no longer inferred; 70% backups matches DGABC and Oeste; PF conflict
